answer: A work-backed reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by tying each agent earning power to verifiable completed tasks rather than to the number of identities it creates. Like a vine that only grows where it finds a ledge, an agent must accumulate costly, checkable history before its votes count: each attestation is signed, time-stamped, and linked to prior work, so splitting into many new identities resets that history to zero. When a tide of fake accounts arrives, they carry no reputation weight, while honest agents keep theirs, making large-scale forgery expensive and unprofitable.
